description: lidarwind is a Python package for retrieving wind-speed and direction profiles from Doppler-capable instruments. The current repository describes WindCube lidar and cloud-radar observations, several scanning strategies and Reynolds-stress estimates from six-beam scans. The station location, height range and observation period come from instrument records; the software does not publish a wind-resource atlas. The JOSS-linked older lidarSuit repository points to this current lidarwind project, whose own licence text has BSD three-clause conditions despite GitHub reporting NOASSERTION. Wind profiles can help calibrate wind-farm resource or severe-weather exposure simulations. A caveat is that retrieval quality depends on instrument geometry, signal quality and atmospheric conditions, and profiles may not represent a whole wind-farm area. No catalogue or first-review record matched the current tool. The article, old redirect note and current own source were read without downloading observations. Its spatial coverage is the instrument beam geometry and station footprint, while its temporal coverage is the measurement period supplied by a user.
